decisions.reason: The citrus harvesting crate is a flagship product built on the firm's core injection-moulded crate know-how, and its agricultural niche is one the firm can interpret and keep refining with its own engineering, though the narrow application adds some risk.

Foldable large containers are central to the firm's returnable packaging expertise, had a dedicated page in both years, and serve automotive and industrial customers where the firm's knowledge base is deepest.
Stackable crates are a core, multi-model line that sits squarely within the firm's existing design and manufacturing knowledge, so it is easy to assimilate feedback and improve the line.
The medium-duty rackable pallet extends the firm's established pallet competence, and its several models suggest ongoing commercial application rather than a one-off trial.

The spill-retention pallet is a more peripheral safety and environmental niche and slipped from its own page to a mere mention, but it still builds on the firm's pallet moulding knowledge and is likely retained as a range filler.

The pallet with load retainers is a single, accessory-like variant whose visibility declined after launch, yet it leverages existing pallet know-how at low cost, so keeping it remains more likely than dropping it.
